title: Bengal Government Strips BJP MP of Banga Bibhushan Award Over Netaji Remarks
excerpt: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari rescinded the state's highest civilian honour from Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Ray after his controversial comments questioning Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's legacy and the Azad Hind Fauj.
body:
• West Bengal government has withdrawn the Banga Bibhushan award from BJP Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Ray (Ananta Maharaj) over remarks deemed insulting to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose
  • CM Suvendu Adhikari ordered police action against those making derogatory comments about the freedom fighter and directed MLAs to set up public service centers named after Netaji
  • Ray had received the award from former CM Mamata Banerjee in February 2026 during Bhasha Diwas celebrations, despite being a BJP MP
  • The controversy has deepened existing faultlines within the BJP's Bengal unit, with Ray previously criticizing his own party for sidelining him

Award Rescinded After Controversial Remarks

The West Bengal government has rescinded the Banga Bibhushan — the state's highest civilian honour — from BJP Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Ray, widely known as Ananta Maharaj. The decision came after Ray made public remarks questioning the legacy of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and the establishment of the Azad Hind Fauj, triggering backlash across political lines.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari ordered the withdrawal of the award and directed law enforcement to take action against individuals making derogatory remarks about the iconic freedom fighter. Adhikari also mandated that BJP MLAs establish public service centers named after Netaji in their constituencies, each receiving Rs 30,000 in monthly state assistance.

"Delete posts, apologise."

— Suvendu Adhikari, West Bengal Chief Minister, directing action against those disparaging Netaji

A Complicated Political History

The withdrawal carries layers of political irony. Ray, a prominent figure in the Greater Cooch Behar movement in North Bengal, had received the Banga Bibhushan from former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee at a Bhasha Diwas event in Kolkata on February 21, 2026. At the time, Banerjee was using the occasion to criticize the BJP and rally support against what she called an "authoritarian" situation in India.

Ray's political trajectory has been marked by shifting allegiances. Despite being a BJP Rajya Sabha MP, he accepted the award from Banerjee and hosted her at his residence, drawing criticism from within his own party. His relationship with the BJP leadership has been fraught — he publicly complained of being sidelined after not being invited to Union Home Minister Amit Shah's administrative meeting at Uttarkanya in Siliguri.

BJP's Internal Faultlines Exposed

The controversy has surfaced deeper tensions within the BJP's Bengal unit, barely two months after the party formed its first government in the state. Ray had previously made headlines by describing Prime Minister Narendra Modi, President Droupadi Murmu, and the Bengal Governor as "Pakistani" and "Bangladeshi" while criticizing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Cooch Behar district.

In a separate incident, a legal notice was served on BJP West Bengal president Samik Bhattacharya over his own remarks concerning Netaji and the All-India Forward Bloc. Advocate Nripendra Krishan Roy issued the notice on behalf of social activist Sunil Halder, alleging the comments were "defamatory, historically unsubstantiated, and injurious to the legacy of one of India's foremost freedom fighters."

Netaji's Legacy in Bengal Politics

Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose remains one of the most revered figures in Indian and particularly Bengali political life. His establishment of the Indian National Army and the Provisional Government of Azad Hind during World War II cemented his status as a towering figure in India's independence movement.

The current controversy underscores how Netaji's legacy continues to be a potent force in Bengal politics. Both the TMC and BJP have historically competed to claim his mantle, with successive governments using the freedom fighter's image to rally public sentiment. The BJP government's swift action against its own MP signals the political costs of being seen as disrespectful toward Bengal's most celebrated son.

Ray has since largely distanced himself from official BJP programmes, focusing instead on events organized by his Greater Cooch Behar organization. The district BJP leadership has declined to comment publicly on the controversy.
